This is ISTA PLV's fork of Nael, at [[https://github.com/ISTA-PLV/nael][github.com/ISTA-PLV/nael]].  It branched from Nael 0.8.3, which Mekeor Melire maintains at [[https://codeberg.org/mekeor/nael][codeberg.org/mekeor/nael]], and adds an infoview, signs in the margin and more; the chapter /This Fork/ says what comes from where.  The ~nael~ package on Melpa is upstream Nael, without these additions.

Nael is a set of packages that extend [[https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/][GNU Emacs]] for the [[https://lean-lang.org][Lean]] language.  It is a radically refactored fork of [[https://github.com/leanprover-community/lean4-mode][Lean4-Mode]] with focus on simplicity, modularity and integration into Emacs' core.

The ~nael~ package defines the major mode.  It also introduces simple and two-sided abbreviations per [[https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Abbrevs.html][Abbrev]] and [[https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/autotype/][Skeleton]] respectively.  It teaches Emacs' built-in [[https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/ Language Server Protocol][LSP]] client [[https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/eglot/][Eglot]] about [[https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/blob/master/src/Lean/Data/Lsp/Extra.lean][Lean-specific LSP-extensions]] and tells [[https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Programming-Language-Doc.html][ElDoc]] to display that information, similar to the “[[https://github.com/leanprover/vscode-lean4/blob/master/vscode-lean4/manual/manual.md#infoview][info view]]” in [[https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=leanprover.lean4][vscode-lean]] that many are familiar with.  Similarly, the separate package ~nael-lsp~ may be installed when [[https://github.com/emacs-lsp/lsp-mode][lsp-mode]] is preferred as LSP client.

* This Fork

** Lineage

- [[https://github.com/leanprover-community/lean4-mode][Lean4-Mode]] is the Lean community's Emacs mode for Lean 4.
- Nael is Mekeor Melire's fork of it, on [[https://codeberg.org/mekeor/nael][Codeberg]] and [[https://melpa.org/#/nael][Melpa]].
- This fork, by ISTA PLV, branched from Nael 0.8.3 (commit =c1d3497= of upstream's =release= branch).  Its version number is still upstream's.
- It takes code from elsewhere: ~nael-eglot.el~'s building of imports (=dependencyBuildMode=) and restarting of files are adapted from Doug Torrance's [[https://github.com/d-torrance/lean4-mode][lean4-mode]]; ~nael-rpc.el~ is derived from that lean4-mode's =lean4-rpc.el=, which is derived from Jan Mas Rovira's [[https://github.com/janmasrovira/neo-lean-mode][neo-lean-mode]]; the Doom Emacs module follows Doom Emacs' own =:lang lean= module.  See /License and Maintenance/ and =NOTICE=.

** What It Adds

- An infoview (~nael-infoview~, =C-c C-i=) that talks to Lean's RPC itself, without a web view: goals and the expected type, with the changes of the tactic at point, folding and filters; subterms described by ElDoc, tooltips and the help buffer =*Nael Help*=, and followed to their definitions; the messages of the line of point, with traces, suggestions to apply and links to the explanations of errors.  Files: ~nael-rpc.el~, ~nael-render.el~, ~nael-infoview.el~, ~nael-infoview-buffer.el~, ~nael-infoview-hover.el~.
- Signs in the left margin for diagnostics, complete proofs, unsolved goals, uses of =sorry= and lines being processed (~nael-margin-mode~, ~nael-margin.el~).
- For Eglot: restarting the current file, which builds its imports once (~nael-eglot-restart-file~, =C-c C-r=); not building imports when a file is opened (~nael-eglot-build-dependencies~); Lean's silent diagnostics and widgets in messages.
- Keys for [[https://github.com/emacs-evil/evil][Evil]] (~nael-evil.el~) and a Doom Emacs module (=doom/lang/nael/=).
- Smaller changes: a better syntax table, also for ElDoc, and macros recognized as such (by Alex Loitzl); the first goal is no longer echoed (~nael-eglot-echo-goal~); a shorter ElDoc delay in Nael buffers (~nael-eldoc-idle-delay~).
- Tests in =test/=: =emacs -Q --batch -l build.el test=, and =test-live= with a Lean installation.
- This fork needs Emacs 30.1, instead of 29.1.

* Get Started

The ~nael~ package on Melpa is upstream Nael, without the additions of this fork.  To install this fork, use ~package-vc~ or a clone of this repository, as the /Installation/ chapter below describes; in Doom Emacs, use its module.

* Usage

Language Server Protocol (LSP):

- =C-c C-e= (~eglot~) starts Eglot, the LSP client.
- =C-c C-r= (~nael-eglot-restart-file~) makes the Lean server reprocess the current file, building its imports first if they are out of date.  Opening a file does not build its imports, unless ~nael-eglot-build-dependencies~ is non-nil.
- =C-c C-i= (~nael-infoview~) toggles the infoview, a window that shows the goals and the expected type at point and follows point.  It needs Lean 4.30 or later.
- =C-h .= (~eldoc-doc-buffer~) displays the ElDoc documentation buffer showing tactic state and expected goal at point, unless the infoview shows them.
- =C-c C-l= (~lsp~) starts lsp-mode, an alternative LSP client.  The key is only bound if ~nael-lsp~ is (auto)loaded.

Signs in the left margin, while Eglot manages the buffer (~nael-margin-mode~):

- =‼= marks the line of an error, =!= that of a warning or a note.  A diagnostic that spans several lines gets a bar over them instead, =┌=, =│=, =└=, in its color.  These are the indicators that Flymake shows otherwise; Flymake still underlines the diagnostics and shows their messages.  The tooltip of a sign shows the message, and clicking it lists all diagnostics.
- =✓= marks a proof that is complete, =✗= the last line of one with unsolved goals, where it goes on, and =⚠= a declaration that uses =sorry=.  Other signs, such as emoji, can be set with ~nael-margin-goals-accomplished~, ~nael-margin-unsolved-goals~ and ~nael-margin-admitted~; with most fonts, an emoji makes its line taller, unless ~nael-margin-emoji-height~ makes it smaller, such as 0.7.
- An orange =│= marks the lines that Lean is still processing.

Infoview:

- In a complete proof, a line above the goals says "Goals accomplished ✓", and replaces "no goals" when none are left.
- Below the goals and the expected type, the section /Messages/ shows Lean's messages on the line of point: errors, warnings, and output such as that of =#check=.  Messages that start on another line, like an error about a whole proof, are folded; messages about the whole file, like that its imports are out of date, are not, and come first.  That message has a =[restart file]= button, which does what =C-c C-r= does.  Their terms are subterms like those of goals.  =RET= or =mouse-1= on the position of a message goes there in the source.
- Traces, as with =set_option trace.Meta.synthInstance true in=, are headings: =TAB= on one shows its children, which Lean sends on request only.
- Suggestions such as Lean's "Try this" have an =[apply]= button that replaces the code in the source with the suggestion; this includes the tactics of libraries that suggest through Lean's =TryThis=.  Lean's hints show the change they suggest as a diff, which applies the same way.  The code of an error, such as =[lean.invalidField]=, opens its explanation in Lean's reference manual.
- =v= (~nael-infoview-view-options~) opens a menu of what the infoview shows: which hypotheses to hide, whether to show the target first and the changes of the tactic at point, and how to show the expected type.

- With [[https://github.com/emacs-evil/evil][Evil]], =(with-eval-after-load 'evil (nael-evil-setup))= binds keys in normal state that don't clash with its motions: =]g= and =[g= for the next and previous goal, =]h= and =[h= for headings, =gr= to refresh, =K= to describe the subterm at point, and, with a local leader, =<localleader> v= for the view options and =<localleader> y= to copy the goal.

Infoview, on a subterm of a goal:

- ElDoc echoes the subterm with all its arguments made explicit, and its type.  With [[https://github.com/casouri/eldoc-box][eldoc-box]], this appears in a popup.
- With ~tooltip-mode~, the tooltip of the subterm under the mouse shows it with its type and documentation.
- =RET=, =mouse-1= or =C-h .= (~nael-infoview-describe~) describes the subterm in the help buffer =*Nael Help*=: its explicit form, its type, its documentation, and how the tactic at point changes it.  Its subterms can be described in turn, and the history goes back and forth: =l= and =r=, or =C-o= and =C-i= with Evil.  In Doom Emacs, =K= describes too.  Closing the help window returns to the infoview.
- =M-.= (~xref-find-definitions~) shows the definition of the subterm in another window, and =M-,= (~xref-go-back~) returns to the infoview.  In Doom Emacs, these are =gd= and =C-o=.

Abbreviations:

- =C-c C-a= (~abbrev-mode~) enables abbreviations.
- =C-c C-k= (~nael-abbrev-help~) echoes abbreviations that expand to the character at point, or, if active, to the selected region.
- =C-x '= (~expand-abbrev~) expands the abbreviation before point without any inserting any character.  (Usually, you'd insert a space or newline to expand.)

Build:

- =C-c C-c= (~project-compile~) prompts for a command to build the current project.  It will suggest =lake build= because Nael configures the ~compile-command~ variable.

Navigation:

- =M-a= (~forward-sentence~) go to beginning of current sentence/block, or to previous one.
- =M-e= (~backward-sentence~) go to end of current sentence/block, or to next one.
- =M-g i= (~imenu~) jumps to an interactively chosen definition in current buffer.

Comments:

- =M-;= (~comment-dwim~) toggles the active region as comment or, if no region is active, creates a comment at end of line.
- =M-q= (~prog-fill-reindent-defun~) fills the string- or comment-paragraph at point, or reindents the point-surrounding code.

* Configuration

To view the complete list of Nael's user option variables from within Emacs, customize the group ~nael~ (and its child-groups) with =M-x customize-group RET nael RET=.  This chapter highlights and elaborates on some of them.

As an exception, Emacs customization groups cannot include keymaps.  You can bind custom keys in ~nael-mode-map~ like this:

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(keymap-set nael-mode-map "C-c ." #'highlight-symbol-at-point)
#+end_src

To automatically enable features (e.g. abbreviations, Eglot or lsp-mode) when Nael is started, customize ~nael-mode-hook~ as follows:

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(add-hook 'nael-mode-hook #'abbrev-mode)
(add-hook 'nael-mode-hook #'eglot-ensure)
#+end_src

The signs in the margin can be changed, also for a single project in its =.dir-locals.el=.  An empty string leaves a sign out; errors and warnings then keep their own.  For example, with chickens:

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(setq nael-margin-goals-accomplished "🐣"  ; complete proof
      nael-margin-unsolved-goals "🥚"      ; unsolved goals
      nael-margin-admitted "🍗"            ; uses sorry
      nael-margin-emoji-height 0.7)        ; as tall as text lines
#+end_src

The margin is as wide as its widest sign.

To keep Flymake's indicators instead of the signs, set ~nael-margin~ to =nil= before opening Lean files.

For the infoview to show messages with their terms, traces and suggestions, Nael asks Lean for them when the project's =lean-toolchain= names Lean 4.30 or later.  Then the text of a trace that Flymake shows is only "(trace)", as in VS Code.  To keep the full text in Flymake instead, set ~nael-eglot-widgets~ to =nil= before Lean starts.

Nael's Abbrev tables use the =:regexp= property which is [[https://github.com/minad/cape/discussions/158#discussioncomment-14687758][incompatible]] with [[https://github.com/company-mode/company-mode][Company]]'s ~company-abbrev~ and [[https://github.com/minad/cape][Cape]]'s ~cape-abbrev~.  Instead, Nael supports completion-at-point natively via ~nael-abbrev-capf~.  This CAPF is buffer-locally added to ~completion-at-point-functions~ whenever Abbrev mode is enabled inside Nael.  To ditch this feature, set the ~nael-abbrev-capf~ variable to =nil=.

* Installation

Nael's LSP-based features (via Eglot or lsp-mode), require Lean version 4 to be [[https://lean-lang.org/install/manual/][installed]].

** Installation from Melpa

~nael~ and ~nael-lsp~ packages are available on [[https://melpa.org/#/nael][Melpa]] (and [[https://stable.melpa.org/#/nael][Melpa-Stable]]).  These are upstream Nael, without the additions of this fork.  To install, first add the package-archive by adding this code to your Emacs initialization file and evaluating it interactively.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(require 'package)
(add-to-list 'package-archives '("melpa" . "https://melpa.org/packages/") t)
(package-initialize)
#+end_src

Then type =M-x package-refresh-contents RET=.  Finally, choose one of the following approaches:  ⦿ To install interactively, type =M-x package-install RET nael RET=.  ⦿ To install via package selection, add =(setopt package-selected-packages '(nael))= to your init file, evaluate it, and type =M-x package-install-selected-packages RET=.  ⦿ To install via Use-Package, add =(use-package nael :ensure t)= to your init file and evaluate it.

** Installation from Sources

The instructions below install this fork.  For upstream Nael, use =https://codeberg.org/mekeor/nael.git= instead.

When installing ~nael-lsp~ from sources, lsp-mode might not be pulled in and installed as dependency automatically, i.e. you might need to install it manually beforehand.

*** Manual Installation

First clone the Git repository, then, in your Emacs initialization file, add Nael to ~load-path~ and load it.  For lazy loading the autoloads-file needs to be build beforehand.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
;; git clone https://github.com/ISTA-PLV/nael.git ~/path/to/nael

(add-to-list 'load-path "~/path/to/nael/nael")
;; (add-to-list 'load-path "~/path/to/nael/nael-lsp")

;; Option 1, eager loading:
(require 'nael)
;; (require 'nael-lsp)

;; Option 2, lazy loading:
;; cd ~/path/to/nael && ./build.el autoloads
;; (require 'nael-autoloads)
;; (require 'nael-lsp-autoloads)

;; Optionally, make readme available as info manual:
(require 'info)
(info-initialize)
(add-to-list 'Info-directory-list "~/path/to/nael/nael")
#+end_src

*** Installation via ~package-vc~

Since version 29 from 2023, Emacs ships with ~package-vc~ which enables the built-in package manager ~package~ to install from version-controlled source repositories.  Keep in mind to regularly upgrade such packages with the command ~package-vc-upgrade~ or ~package-vc-upgrade-all~.  (And please ignore the warnings that arise when ~package-vc~ attempts to byte-compile all Elisp source files in the repository instead of just the package-specific ones.)

**** Installation via ~package-vc-selected-packages~

In your Emacs session, select packages per ~package-vc-selected-packages~ variable and install them with =M-x package-vc-install-selected-packages RET=.  Persist the package selection in your Emacs initialization file too.  ~package-vc~ will generate the autoloads-file automatically.  To lazy-load Nael, load the autoloads-file.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(require 'package-vc)

(setopt package-vc-selected-packages
        '((nael
           :doc "nael/README.org"
           :lisp-dir "nael"
           :url "https://github.com/ISTA-PLV/nael.git")
       ;; (nael-lsp
       ;;  :lisp-dir "nael-lsp"
       ;;  :url "https://github.com/ISTA-PLV/nael.git")
          ))

(package-initialize)

;; Option 1, lazy loading:
(require 'nael-autoloads)
;; (require 'nael-lsp-autoloads)

;; Option 2, eager loading:
;; (require 'nael)
;; (require 'nael-lsp)
#+end_src

**** Installation via ~use-package~ =:vc=

Since version 30 from 2025, Emacs' popular ~use-package~ macro supports a =:vc= keyword as interface to ~package-vc~.  (Because each package has autoload-cookies on relevant expressions, and because ~use-package~ will load the autoloads-file that is generated at installation, you don't need to specify load-triggers like =:mode=.  I.e. lazy-loading should work out of the box.)

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(use-package nael
  :vc ( :doc "nael/README.org"
        :lisp-dir "nael"
        :url "https://github.com/ISTA-PLV/nael.git"))

;; (use-package nael-lsp
;;   :after nael
;;   :vc ( :lisp-dir "nael-lsp"
;;         :url "https://github.com/ISTA-PLV/nael.git"))
#+end_src

** Installation in Doom Emacs

The repository contains a Doom Emacs module, =:lang nael=, in =doom/lang/nael/=.  It installs this fork of Nael and sets up its infoview, with keys under =SPC m= and for Evil, and replaces Doom's =:lang lean= module.  See its =README.org= for how to install it.

* Changelog

** This fork, not released yet

- Based on Nael 0.8.3.  For what it adds, see /What It Adds/ in the chapter /This Fork/.  The versions below are upstream Nael's.

** Version 0.8.2 from 2026-02-22

- Improved rules for Font-Lock: Highlight identifiers in their definitions.  For example, in “def foo : Nat := 123”, =foo= will be highlighted (via Font-Lock).

** Version 0.8.0 from 2026-12-16

- Fix bugs related to automatic abbreviation expansion:
- Backslash-dot-space now correctly expands to middledot-space, all while the cursor is positioned after the space character.
- Adjacent abbreviations expand correctly, i.e. backslash-dot-backslash expands the first abbreviation, resulting in middledot-backslash.
- Two abbreviations have been dropped, namely backslash and plus-space.

** Version 0.7.0 from 2025-12-15

- Remove the ~nael-markdown~ package.  Move its code into ~nael~ package instead.  (Wrapped into ~with-eval-after-load~.)
- ~nael~ is now on [[https://melpa.org/#/nael][Melpa]] and [[https://stable.melpa.org/#/nael][Melpa-Stable]].  ~nael-lsp~ is not there yet.  (Addendum: ~nael-lsp~ is available on Melpa (and Melpa-Stable) too, since )

** Version 0.6.2 from 2025-11-30

- Re-add readme as .texi and .info to repository because Nael might soon be added to Melpa which won't build Info manuals itself.

** Version 0.6.0 from 2025-11-30

- Remove .texi, .info, and -autoloads.el files from repository.  Thus, don't load autoloads-files from other Elisp sources.  This makes Nael compatible with package-vc.
- build.el: Only build files/targets passed as command-line arguments.  Valid arguments are abbreviations, autoloads, compile, info and root-readme.
- dir-locals.el: Remove an assignment of a non-core Emacs variable which lead to Emacs asking for confirmation.
- README: Provide installation instructions via package-vc-selected-packages and use-package :vc.
- Add several autoload-cookies.  This allows for simpler use-package expressions.
- README: Add changelog chapter.
- nael, nael-abbrev:
  - Rename nael-abbrev-table-only-singletons to nael-abbrev-singleton-table.
  - Rename nael-abbrev-table-only-skeletons to nael-abbrev-skeleton-table.

The files that this fork adds are licensed under GPL-3.0-only, except ~nael-rpc.el~. The Doom Emacs module follows Doom Emacs' =:lang lean= module, under the MIT License.  The test fixtures are recorded from [[https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean][iris-lean]], under Apache-2.0.  For details, see =NOTICE= and =test/fixtures/README.org=.
